specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** capstone-roadmap-poster
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify which of the six capstone stages matches each of six descriptions, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Capstone Project, Improvement Challenge, A/B Test, Publishing OER, Certificate Submission (defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapters 15, 16, and 18). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the poster zone that matches each description. A click is correct when the zone's id equals the Correct zone column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Hovering a zone in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The capstone ends with the improved resource. (2) Testing with students is optional. (3) Sharing means only posting a link. **Instructional Rationale:** Remembering the stages of the capstone and what each asks is a Remember-level task, and a poster with six panels in order lets the learner hold the whole project at once. The quiz asks for the stage by its purpose. **Content:** The poster is a flat illustration of six equal panels in two rows of three, read left to right and top to bottom. Each panel shows one simple pictogram and a stage number, and the printed text is limited to the six stage numbers. The first panel shows a magnifying glass over a page with ten bars. The second shows a robot head with a check mark. The third shows a wrench over a page. The fourth shows two groups of figures joined by an arrow. The fifth shows a globe with a branching line. The sixth shows a speech bubble between two figures. All other words come from the explore and quiz data. The six zones: | Zone id | Label | Summary | Facts shown on hover or click | |---|---|---|---| | stage-1-evaluate | 1. Evaluate | Score your resource on all ten metrics with evidence. | Use the rubric and an agent. Record evidence for each score. Check the license first. | | stage-2-check | 2. Check the agent | Verify the agent's claims and log your findings. | Look for invented citations, misread licenses, and overconfident scores. Accept, correct, or reject each claim. | | stage-3-improve | 3. Improve | Raise at least two quality and two reusability metrics. | Plan lowest first. Review and log every change. Re-score all ten metrics. | | stage-4-test | 4. Test with students | Compare the original and improved versions. | State a hypothesis. Assign by chance. Get consent and protect privacy. Report the effect size and the limits. | | stage-5-publish | 5. Publish | Release the improved resource under CC BY. | Package the components. Include metadata. Build and deploy. Open a feedback channel. | | stage-6-share | 6. Share | Report what you found and help others. | Write the results summary. Track reuse. Offer to train a colleague. | The six quiz questions, in this order: | # | Question | Correct zone | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Which stage asks you to compare an original and an improved version with students? | stage-4-test | The test is the stage with groups and consent. | | 2 | Which stage checks for invented citations and misread licenses? | stage-2-check | Verifying the agent's claims is stage 2. | | 3 | Which stage ends with the resource at a public address under CC BY? | stage-5-publish | Publishing releases the resource. | | 4 | Which stage plans fixes lowest metric first? | stage-3-improve | The plan and the re-score belong to stage 3. | | 5 | Which stage begins with scoring all ten metrics? | stage-1-evaluate | The baseline comes first. | | 6 | Which stage includes offering to train a colleague? | stage-6-share | Sharing includes teaching others. | **Provenance:** The six stages follow the chapter section "Capstone Project" and the course description's capstone. The illustration is synthetic, and it carries no statistics. **Rules:** Each question has exactly one correct zone. Zones are distinct regions of the poster, so a click belongs to at most one zone. Because the poster prints only stage numbers, the sim shows the zone labels on hover. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a panel and reads its summary and facts. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows question 1 above the poster. 3. The learner clicks the panel they think matches. 4. The sim shows the Why text and moves to the next question, until question 6 is done. **Feedback:** 6 questions in the fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The answer is [label]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You know the road to the capstone." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed question. **Starting State:** The poster with no zone selected, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a panel to learn about the stage." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of seven capstone steps groups into these six stages, with the last step combining the report and the offer to train.
